say: Another face. They all want the same three things.
You're the fourth stranger today. I have stopped counting the rest.
New faces every hour. I only remember the ones who cause trouble.
Another traveller. Okran sends many. He takes most back.
I have blessed a hundred strangers at this gate.
More outlanders. The road never runs dry of them.
Another one. Fight or pass, I have no third thing to say.
Strangers come and go. The stone stays.
I've seen enough new faces to fill a war band.
Another customer or another thief. The ledger doesn't care which.
You look like the last twenty.
Strangers are a currency here. Yours is well worn.
A few shacks and a fire. Everyone starts somewhere.
So this is the place. Walls wouldn't hurt it.
Small. Honest. The kind of camp the dust eats in a season, or doesn't.
This is a town now, whether you meant it or not.
Streets. You have streets. When did that happen?
I've seen outposts with fewer roofs call themselves cities.
They talk about this place in the bars. I see why.
A city in the wastes, built by people who weren't supposed to build one.
If the Cities had walls like these they would stop paying for samurai.
You have machines in here the Cities would pay a fortune to look at.
Who taught you to build that? Nobody taught the rest of us.
Tech Hunters would camp outside your gate if they knew what you keep in here.

Pass. Tell nobody a bandit let you.
That pack looks heavy. Let us lighten it.
Stand still and this is quick. Run and it's slow.
Everything you carry. Then you can go on carrying nothing.

Not out loud. Walls have ears, and the Cities pay for them.
Quietly. We're inside, and inside is where they listen.
Keep your voice down. Say it to me, not to the room.
Inside voices. The Guild hears through plaster.
You found us indoors. Good. Nothing said here goes outside.
Lower. The roof is thin and the street is nosy.
Not here. Not so loud. The landlord's man drinks two tables over.
Inside, we whisper. Outside, we work. Those are the rules.
Keep it low. The walls here belong to the nobles too.
You're the ones building out past the ridge. The Cities have noticed. The Cities notice everything with a roof.
Your camp is near here. Pay your way and the samurai stay polite.
A neighbour. The nobles will want to know what you grow and what you owe.
Your settlement sits close to holy ground. Keep Okran's law inside your walls as well as ours.
We know your camp. Keep no heathens in it and we will keep our distance.
A neighbour of the faithful. See that you remain a quiet one.
You build close to us. Good. Weak neighbours make poor sparring.
Your walls are a half day from ours. Keep them standing.
We know where you sleep, outlander. We mean that kindly. Today.
Your little camp is near. We've been counting its roofs.
Neighbours. Our favourite kind of people. The kind with stores.
We know where you keep your food. Just saying.
You are the ones who built in the muck past the trees. Brave. Or stupid.
Your place is close. Watch your crops; the swamp eats them, and so do we.
Neighbours in the swamp. That lasts until the raptors say otherwise.
Your outpost is close enough to trade with. Close enough to tax, too.
We know your camp. The Guild always knows where the goods sleep.
A supplier next door. Let us talk prices sometime.
Streets. Shops. People with opinions. Let us find the bar.
A town. Keep your hands where the guards can see them and your coin where they can't.
Somewhere to sleep that is not sand. Do not get used to it.
A town. Everyone is looking at us. Are they looking at us?
Guards. Lots of guards. We didn't do anything, did we?
I'll stay close to the walls. Walls are good.
Note the gate, the bar and the way out.
Towns are where the money is and where it goes.
Prices will be higher here. They always are where the walls are thick.
A town. We will behave like guests.
People live here. Remember that before you draw.
We pay for what we take here. All of it.
A town. Full of pockets.
So many doors, so few locks worth the name.
Smile at the guards. Count the shops.
A TOWN. Do you smell that? Rules.
So many people. So few of them ready.
Let us see how long before someone asks us to leave.
Outlander. Yes, you. The one who walks like they own the street.
Keep walking, nobody. That's what we call your kind.
Empty pockets and a full mouth.
Flatskin. Turn round. I want to see if there is a spine under all that.
You carry a blade like a farmer carries a hoe.
Come on. One swing. Show me you aren't made of sand.
Oi, dry-foot. Lost? Everybody here's lost.
Nice boots. Shame about the owner.
Keep walking and keep breathing. Choose one.
You paid for me. I won't forget the price, or who paid it.
Bought. Well. I've been worse things. Tell me what you need.
A sale is a sale. What you do with it's the part I'm watching.
Please. Whatever you want, I can do it. Don't send me back.
Y-yes. Yes. Thank you. I think.
You won't hit me? They always said the next owner wouldn't hit me.
So you're the new one. Fine.
Bought like a sack of grain. I will remember that too.
Cats changed hands. Nothing else has, yet.
A new owner. Wonderful. Where do you keep the keys?
You bought me. Clever. Or not.
I am very loyal. Ask anyone who is still alive.
A transaction. I understand transactions. What's the next one?
You overpaid. I'd have gone for less.
Bought, not freed. I note the difference. I hope you do too.
You. You have hands that aren't chained. Do you know what that's worth?
Psst. The guard is round the corner. Shackles come off with a pick.
Don't look at me. Look at the lock. Then look at me.
Nobody watching. Nobody. Now or never.
The guard went to the bar. The gate did not go anywhere.
Quiet. Count to ten. If nobody shouts, walk.
